lesson.title: Rank and null space

steps.headline: The rank counts a matrix's independent outputs. The null space holds the inputs it sends to zero.

lead.text: The column space is every output A v. Its dimension is the rank, which is the number of pivots. The null space is every input with A v = 0, and its dimension is the nullity.
The null space holds the inputs that A sends to zero. Here A is $\begin{pmatrix}1&2&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$. Dot each row with the input to test one.

reveal.text: You dotted the first row with the input, and it vanished. That input is in the null space, since the second row vanishes too.

steps.headline: Find the rank and nullity of $\begin{pmatrix}1&3&0&2\\0&0&1&4\end{pmatrix}$.

workedSteps.text: The matrix is already reduced. There are pivots in columns 1 and 3.
The matrix has 4 columns. The nullity is the columns that are left over.
Row 1 has its first nonzero entry in column 1. Row 2 has its first nonzero entry in column 3.
Count the pivots. What is the rank?

lead.text: The matrix A is $\begin{pmatrix}1&2&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$. It has three columns, and you know its rank.

reveal.text: You took the rank away from the number of columns. Each column without a pivot is a free direction, and those directions are the null space.

lead.text: The column space is built from columns of the original matrix. The pivot columns show which of them are independent.

lesson.orientation: Connect pivot columns, column space and the inputs a matrix sends to zero.
lesson.nextAction: Try the next idea, then return for a fresh problem after a delay.

blocks.text: A machine takes a point (x, y) and gives back the number x + y. The point (2, −2) goes to 0.

intro.promise: By the end you'll count a matrix's rank and nullity, and say which inputs it sends to zero.

recap.keyIdea: The rank counts the independent output directions and the nullity counts the inputs sent to zero. Together they add up to the number of columns.

blocks.text: You found rank 2 and nullity 1 for the same three-column matrix, checked that (−2, 1, 0) is sent to zero, and chose columns 1 and 3 as a basis.

recap.nextHook: Maps also stretch area. Next: the determinant, and why zero means a collapse.

questions.prompt: For x = 5, what value of y also gives the output 0?
hints: The output is x + y. What must y be for it to vanish?
The two numbers must cancel.
What number added to five gives zero?

misconceptions.feedback: The sign is missing. The two numbers must cancel, so they must have opposite signs.

questions.onCorrect: −5. Every point (x, −x) goes to zero. Inputs sent to zero are what the null space collects.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Rank plus nullity is 5, so the nullity is 5 − 2 = 3.

questions.prompt: A matrix has 5 columns and rank 2. What is its nullity?
hints: Rank plus nullity equals the number of columns.
Which two numbers do you already have?
Take the rank away from the number of columns.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the rank. The nullity is what is left of the columns.
That adds the two numbers. Subtract the rank from the columns.

questions.prompt: For A = $\begin{pmatrix}1&2&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$, what is the first coordinate of A(−2, 1, 0)?
hints: Use the first row of A.
Multiply each entry of the row by the matching input entry, then add.
The two nonzero products have opposite signs.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The first row gives −2 + 2 = 0; the second output is also zero.

misconceptions.feedback: That is only the first product. Add the second product as well.

questions.onCorrect: The products cancel. An input that A sends to zero lies in the null space.

acceptedIdeas: Each pivot column fixes one unknown, and the other columns are free.
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Pivot columns are fixed by the others. The remaining columns are free directions in the null space.

questions.prompt: Why is the nullity the number of columns minus the rank?

choices.label: Each pivot column fixes one unknown, and the other columns are free.
The null space has as many vectors as the matrix has rows.

hints: Which columns can take any value?

misconceptions.feedback: Only for matrices that send nothing but zero to zero. Many matrices collapse some inputs.
Rows do not decide it. The columns and their pivots do.

questions.onCorrect: Pivot columns are fixed by the others, so the leftover columns are the free ones.

questions.prompt: What is the rank of A = $\begin{pmatrix}1&2&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$?
hints: Rank is the number of pivots.
Where does each row have its first nonzero entry?
Count the pivot columns.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: There is a pivot in the first and third columns, giving rank two.

misconceptions.feedback: That counts all the columns. Rank counts only the pivot columns.

questions.onCorrect: Rank is the number of pivots: columns 1 and 3 each have one.

questions.prompt: What is the nullity of A = $\begin{pmatrix}1&2&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$?
hints: Rank plus nullity equals the number of columns.
The matrix has three columns and rank two.
Take the rank away from the number of columns.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: A has three columns and rank two, so nullity is 3 − 2 = 1.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the rank. Nullity is the number of columns minus the rank.
That counts all the columns. Take the rank away.

questions.onCorrect: Three columns less rank two leaves nullity one: one free direction.

questions.prompt: Which pair of columns of A = $\begin{pmatrix}1&2&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$ is a basis for its column space?
hints: Which columns hold the pivots?

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Columns 1 and 3 hold the pivots. Column 2 is twice column 1.

misconceptions.feedback: Column 2 is twice column 1, so that pair is redundant. Choose the pivot columns.

questions.onCorrect: The pivot columns of the original matrix give a basis for the column space.

hints: Rank is the number of pivots.
Which diagonal entries are nonzero?
Count them.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: All three diagonal entries are nonzero, so there are three pivots.

misconceptions.feedback: That multiplies the diagonal entries. Rank counts the pivots.

questions.onCorrect: Each nonzero diagonal entry is a pivot, and there are three of them.

hints: Is either row a multiple of the other?
Find the rank first, then take it away from the number of columns.
The matrix has three columns.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The second row is redundant; rank is one and there are three columns, so nullity is two.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the rank. Nullity is the number of columns minus the rank.
That counts all the columns. Take the rank away.

questions.onCorrect: The second row repeats the first, so the rank is one. Three columns less one is two.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The second column is twice the first, so there is only a single pivot.

hints: Compare the two columns.
Is either column a multiple of the other?
Count the independent columns.

misconceptions.feedback: The columns look different, but each is a multiple of the other. Count independent ones.
That is the number of rows. Rank counts independent columns.

questions.onCorrect: The second column is twice the first, so only one column is independent.
